NONE: › to give a weak form of a disease to a person or animal, usually by injection, as a protection against that disease

example: My children have been inoculated against polio.
我的孩子都打了小兒麻痺預防針。

NONE: › not causing any harm or offence
（尤指人或其行為）無害的，不冒犯人的

example: an inoffensive article
不得罪人的文章
He seemed like a quiet, inoffensive sort of a guy.
他看上去像一個安靜隨和的人。

NONE: › If a tumour (= a growth) or other medical condition is inoperable, doctors are unable to remove or treat it with an operation.
（腫瘤等）不宜動手術的，手術不能治癒的
› If a system, plan, machine, etc. is inoperable, it cannot be done or made to work.
（系統、計劃、機器等）無法操作的，行不通的，不能實行的
› (of a law, rule, etc.) not having effect or power, or (of a machine, system, etc.) not working or not able to work as usual
（法律、規章等）無效力的；（機器、系統等）不工作的，不能正常運轉的

example: The old regulations became inoperative when the new ones were issued.
新規則公佈後，舊規則隨即失效。
There were guidelines about the procedure to follow if any of the voting machines became inoperative.
指南規定了在投票機不能工作時應該遵守的程序。

NONE: › happening or done at a time that is not suitable or convenient

example: I'm sorry, you've called at an inopportune moment.
對不起，你的電話來得不是時候。

NONE: › much more than usual or expected

example: Margot has always spent an inordinate amount of time on her appearance.
瑪戈總是花太多時間打扮自己。

NONE: › not being or consisting of living material, or (of chemical substances) containing no carbon or only small amounts of carbon

example: Salt is an inorganic chemical.
鹽是無機化學物質。
The meteorites contained only inorganic material.
這些隕石只含有無機物。
